title: Frontend Developer
summary: Frontend developers build the parts of a website or web app that people see and use, such as pages, buttons, forms and menus, using HTML, CSS and JavaScript. The role suits students who care about both clean code and a good, accessible experience for users.

sources.title: 12 In-Demand Front End Developer Skills – roadmap.sh
Full Stack JavaScript Path – The Odin Project

nodes.title: How the web and browsers work
nodes.summary: Learn how a browser asks a server for a page, what HTML, CSS and JavaScript each do, and how to set up an editor and browser developer tools. This makes every later step easier to follow.

resources.title: How the web works – MDN Web Docs

nodes.proof: Explain, using your browser's developer tools, what files a real website loads and roughly what each one does.

nodes.title: Semantic HTML
nodes.summary: Use the right HTML element for each job: headings, lists, links, buttons, forms and landmarks. Good structure helps screen readers, search engines and your own CSS.
nodes.proof: Build a multi-page site with a working form, using only semantic HTML, that passes the W3C HTML validator.

nodes.title: CSS, layout and responsive design
nodes.summary: Style pages with CSS, including the box model, Flexbox, Grid and media queries, so layouts work on small phones and large screens. Many users in India browse mainly on phones, so test small widths first.
nodes.proof: Recreate the layout of a real website's home page that adapts cleanly from 360px phone width to desktop.

sources.title: Responsive Web Design certification redesigned – freeCodeCamp

nodes.title: Accessibility
nodes.summary: Make sites usable for everyone, including people using a keyboard or screen reader: labels on form fields, enough colour contrast, visible focus and meaningful alt text. It is a core skill, not an extra.
nodes.proof: Use one of your sites with only the keyboard, fix every problem you find, and list the fixes in the README.

sources.title: 12 In-Demand Front End Developer Skills – roadmap.sh

nodes.title: JavaScript and the DOM
nodes.summary: Learn JavaScript properly: variables, functions, arrays, objects, events, changing the page through the DOM, and async code with promises and fetch. It is the main language of frontend work.

resources.title: Full Stack JavaScript Path – The Odin Project

nodes.proof: Build a weather or movie search app in plain JavaScript that calls a public API and handles loading and error states.

nodes.title: Git and GitHub
nodes.summary: Track every project with Git, use branches, and share code on GitHub. Recruiters often look at your GitHub, and teams use pull requests to review each other's work.

resources.title: The Missing Semester of Your CS Education – MIT

nodes.proof: Every project is on GitHub with a README, small clear commits, and at least one merged pull request.

nodes.title: A framework (React) and TypeScript
nodes.summary: Learn one framework such as React: components, props, state, effects and routing. Then add TypeScript, a typed version of JavaScript that catches mistakes early and is common in team codebases.

resources.title: Full Stack JavaScript Path – The Odin Project
CS50's Web Programming with Python and JavaScript

nodes.proof: Rebuild your plain JavaScript app in React with routing, shared state and at least one form, then convert it to TypeScript.

nodes.title: APIs, testing and performance
nodes.summary: Fetch and send data to REST APIs, write tests for your components, and learn to find slow parts of a page using browser tools. These separate a demo from work a team can trust.

resources.title: Overview of HTTP – MDN Web Docs
12 In-Demand Front End Developer Skills – roadmap.sh

nodes.proof: Add tests for the main user flows of your React app and record one page-load improvement you made with before and after numbers.

sources.title: 12 In-Demand Front End Developer Skills – roadmap.sh

nodes.title: Two or three deployed portfolio projects
nodes.summary: Build a small set of polished, live projects that show different skills, such as a responsive site, an API-driven app and a React app with forms and tests. Quality matters more than quantity.
nodes.proof: Two or three live links, each with a public repo, screenshots, and a README that explains what you built and why.

sources.title: What You Can Do to Prepare – The Odin Project

nodes.title: Interviews and applying
nodes.summary: Read real frontend job descriptions to see what is asked, prepare to explain your projects and core HTML, CSS and JavaScript ideas, and practise small live-coding tasks. Apply steadily and follow up.

resources.title: Preparing to Interview and Interviewing – The Odin Project
Applying for Web Development Jobs – The Odin Project

nodes.proof: A portfolio page, a one-page resume, and three mock interviews where you build a small UI component live.
